summary: Parcus reports managing 18 car parks with about 10,000 spaces in Strasbourg, and in June 2026 Parcus+ took over the Wodli and Gare courte durée station car parks; since 1 December 2025 paid on-street parking has been run by the public company SPL Parcus+voirie, replacing Streeteo. Paid on-street parking was extended to Neudorf in June 2024, the Crit'Air 3 restriction in the low-emission zone was moved to January 2027, and in June 2026 the city council cut resident permits to 5, 10 and 20 euros a month and capped visitor tariffs at 17 euros from September 2026. Tram F's extension to Wolfisheim, with a 100-space P+R, opened in November 2025, and the 2025 Christmas market drew 3.05 million visitors against a record 3.4 million the year before.

items.text: Paid on-street parking was extended to the Neudorf district from 1 June 2024, after a city council vote in March 2023. The new paid area is a green tariff zone with a 5-hour limit, charged 9:00-19:00 Monday to Saturday, and residents can choose a Résipark garage subscription at 60 or 90 euros a month.
items.source_title: Quartier Neudorf : nouvelles zones de stationnement payant à compter du 1er juin 2024

items.text: The Eurométropole announced that it was extending the education-only phase of its low-emission zone, so Crit'Air 3 vehicles may keep driving in it until 31 December 2026 instead of being banned from 2025. Strasbourg was one of a few cities to get a two-year exemption from the ministry.
items.source_title: ZFE : Strasbourg reporte l'interdiction de circulation des voitures Crit'Air 3

items.text: The city's ZFE-m page lists Crit'Air 5 vehicles as restricted from January 2023 and Crit'Air 4 from January 2024, with Crit'Air 3 restrictions scheduled for January 2027 and Crit'Air 2 for January 2028. The Crit'Air 2 step has so far been decided only by Strasbourg, Schiltigheim, Ostwald and Holtzheim, and the page says the timetable may be adjusted after air-quality reviews.
items.source_title: ZFE|m : Mieux respirer c'est ça l'idée !! | Strasbourg.eu

items.text: Parliament voted in April 2026 to abolish low-emission zones nationwide as part of an economic simplification law. On 21 May 2026 the Constitutional Council struck that provision down on procedural grounds, so the zones, including Strasbourg's, remain in place.
items.source_title: Fin des ZFE ? Suppression votée puis censurée : ce qui change en 2026

items.text: A new public local company, SPL Parcus+voirie, took over Strasbourg's paid on-street parking on 1 December 2025 under a 15-year contract, replacing Streeteo, which had held the contract since 2018. Its capital is public: 95% City of Strasbourg and 5% Eurométropole. The EasyPark and Indigo Neo payment apps were kept, and a new Parcus+ app was announced for 2026.
items.source_title: La SPL Parcus+voirie reprend le service du stationnement payant sur voirie à Strasbourg

items.text: On 22 June 2026 the city council voted to cut monthly on-street resident permits from 15, 30 and 40 euros to 5, 10 and 20 euros (tiers set by household income), effective 1 July 2026. From 1 September 2026 visitor tariffs were capped at 17 euros for the maximum stay (3 hours red zone, 4 hours orange, 5 hours green); the post-parking charge is 17 euros if paid within three days and 35 euros after that.
items.source_title: Stationnement : les forfaits résidents divisés par deux ou trois

items.text: CTS lists 12 park-and-ride sites with more than 4,000 spaces in total. A day ticket costs 4.20 euros and covers parking plus unlimited bus and tram travel for 1 to 7 people; longer stays cost 7.20 euros for 24 hours, 14.40 for 48 hours and 21.60 for 72 hours. CTS season-ticket holders park free at every site except Rotonde, which has its own 66-euro monthly pass.

Parcus says 137 charge points across 12 Parcus+ car parks are available, run by Freshmile, including Gutenberg, Austerlitz, Broglie, Wodli and Gare courte durée. Since August 2022 the price in most of these car parks has been 0.50 euros per session plus 0.60 euros per kWh, on top of the parking fee; a separate tariff has applied at Wodli and Gare courte durée since 10 June 2026.
items.source_title: Borne de recharge pour les véhicules électriques - Parcus

items.text: Parcus says it manages 18 car parks (17 underground and one enclosed) with about 10,000 spaces in total. In 2023 these car parks handled more than 3 million hourly customers and more than 7,500 subscription contracts.
items.source_title: Parcus - L'art de vivre la ville

items.text: On 10 June 2026 Parcus+ took over operation of the Wodli car park beside Strasbourg station (955 spaces on 11 levels, 42 with EV charging) and the station's VéloParc bike park.
items.source_title: Parking Wodli et Véloparc de la gare - Parcus

items.text: The Gare courte durée car park, closed since a fire on 1 May, reopened to the public after a safety commission gave a favourable opinion on 23 July 2026, with repair works nearly complete. Parcus+ had taken over its operation on 10 June.

The Eurométropole publishes an open dataset of available spaces in its multi-storey and underground car parks, refreshed every 3 minutes under the Etalab Open Licence. On the research date it held 35 records.
items.source_title: Occupation en temps réel des parkings

items.text: Tram line F was scheduled to run along eight new stations between Strasbourg, Eckbolsheim and Wolfisheim from 15 November 2025. The park-and-ride at the Wolfisheim Henri-Rendu terminus has 100 car spaces and 50 bike spaces.
items.source_title: Avec l'extension du tram F, les mobilités se redessinent à l'ouest

items.text: The Eurométropole reported that use of all its park-and-ride sites rose during the 2025 Christmas market and that the new Wolfisheim P+R (100 spaces, open since 15 November) had high daily occupancy. It said it was examining P+R use and, for Wolfisheim, would measure how much was due to the Christmas peak before taking adapted measures if needed.
items.source_title: Le succès des parkings-relais de l'Eurométropole en période de fêtes

items.text: For the 2025 Christmas market, on-street parking was banned around the clock across the Grande-Île from 22:00 on 25 November. The official Christmas site pointed visitors to the 12 park-and-ride sites at 4.20 euros.
items.source_title: How to park? | Noël à Strasbourg

items.text: A local guide reported that during the 2025 Christmas market (26 November to 24 December) the Grande-Île would be closed to general traffic. It also said the Kléber, Gutenberg and Broglie car parks would be closed to the public and kept for holders of a special access pass.
items.source_title: Tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur le merveilleux Marché de Noël de Strasbourg cette année

items.text: The city reported 3.05 million visitors to the 2025 Christmas market, below the record 3.4 million of 2024. About half of visitors lived in the Eurométropole, and hotel occupancy was close to 90%, with guests from Germany among other markets.
items.source_title: Strasbourg Capitale de Noël a attiré plus de 3 millions de personnes
